questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 6 cm and height 14 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2(3.14)(36) + 2(3.14)(6)(14) = 226.1 + 527.5 = 753.6 cm². A common error is forgetting the two circular ends (giving 527.5) or only including one end (376.8).

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Weimar Republic's system of proportional representation meant that even tiny fringe parties could win seats in the Reichstag. What was the main practical consequence of this?
options: Coalition governments were unstable and often collapsed quickly
Only the Nazi party was allowed to hold seats
Voting became compulsory for all German citizens
The president automatically gained more power each election
questions.answer: Coalition governments were unstable and often collapsed quickly
questions.why: Because seats matched vote share almost exactly, no single party usually won a majority, forcing fragile multi-party coalitions that frequently broke down — a key weakness of Weimar democracy.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: By the early 1930s, millions of unemployed Germans were losing faith in the mainstream parties that had governed through the Depression. Which statement best explains why this specifically helped the Nazis rather than just making people angry in general?
options: The Nazis offered clear scapegoats and promised strong, decisive leadership when other parties seemed unable to act
The Nazis were the only party allowed to campaign during the Depression
Unemployment automatically made people vote for whichever party was largest
The Depression had no real effect on which party people supported
questions.answer: The Nazis offered clear scapegoats and promised strong, decisive leadership when other parties seemed unable to act
questions.why: Correlation isn't causation: it wasn't just that hardship existed, but that the Nazis actively channelled that despair into simple explanations and confident promises, which mainstream parties failed to offer.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Two historians debate Australia's post-WWII migration: one says it was driven purely by government economic planning, the other says it was purely about migrants' personal choices. Which response best captures the fuller picture?
options: It was a combination of Australia's push for labour and population growth alongside migrants' own push and pull factors like escaping hardship or seeking opportunity
It was entirely planned by the government with no input from migrants themselves
It was entirely due to individual migrants' choices, with no government involvement at all
It only happened because of the White Australia Policy encouraging global migration
questions.answer: It was a combination of Australia's push for labour and population growth alongside migrants' own push and pull factors like escaping hardship or seeking opportunity
questions.why: Real historical explanations rarely rest on a single cause — Australia's policy needs and migrants' personal motivations worked together, not as opposing forces.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.prompt: A student writing a business plan for a new bakery lists these two items: 'a competitor bakery is opening two streets away' and 'flour prices are rising this year'. Both are genuine external threats. Which section should this information go in — SWOT analysis or market analysis?
options: SWOT analysis
Market analysis
Executive summary
Both sections equally, since threats can appear anywhere
questions.why: Threats (like a new competitor or rising costs) are one of the four letters in SWOT — Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats — so external risks like these belong there, not in market analysis, which is about researching customers, competitors' prices, and demand as background data. The misconception is thinking any mention of a competitor or cost automatically means 'market analysis' — it depends on whether it's being analysed as a risk/opportunity (SWOT) or just described as market data.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: When the body encounters a pathogen it has met before, memory cells trigger a much faster antibody response the second time. What is this ability called?
options: Immunity
Inflammation
Digestion
Circulation
questions.why: Immunity is the body's ability to resist a pathogen it has previously encountered, thanks to memory cells 'remembering' it and enabling a faster, stronger response next time.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A city's population grows quickly as people move from rural farms to work in city factories, while at the same time a family moves permanently from another country to start a new life there. Which statement correctly separates these two processes?
options: The factory workers are urbanising within their own country; the family is migrating between countries
Both groups are migrating, since both are moving to a new place
Both groups are urbanising, since both end up living in a city
The factory workers are migrating; the family is urbanising
questions.answer: The factory workers are urbanising within their own country; the family is migrating between countries
questions.why: Urbanisation is internal movement from rural to urban areas within the same country; migration is movement across a border into a new country — the two are easily confused but describe different kinds of movement.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 17 cm and a height of 8 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?
options: 68 cm²
136 cm²
25 cm²
102 cm²
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 17 × 8 = 68 cm². Multiplying base × height without halving gives the rushed wrong answer of 136 cm² — always pause and apply the ½ deliberately.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 8 cm and height 5 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2(3.14)(64) + 2(3.14)(8)(5) = 401.9 + 251.2 = 653.1 cm². Forgetting either the two circular ends or the curved side gives an incomplete total.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Weimar Republic's constitution allowed the president to bypass parliament and rule by emergency decree under Article 48. Why did this weaken the republic's stability long-term?
options: It normalised rule without parliamentary approval, making it easier for future leaders to seize power without real democratic consent
It gave ordinary citizens the power to overrule the president directly
It abolished elections completely from 1919 onwards
It only applied to foreign policy decisions, not domestic ones
questions.answer: It normalised rule without parliamentary approval, making it easier for future leaders to seize power without real democratic consent
questions.why: Article 48 was meant for emergencies, but repeated use eroded the norm of parliamentary government, paving the way for Hitler to later use similar emergency powers to dismantle democracy entirely.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why the Great Depression strengthened the Nazi party specifically, rather than simply making Germans generally frustrated with politics?
options: The Nazis directly blamed identifiable groups and promised concrete solutions, giving desperate voters a clear alternative other parties didn't offer
The Depression affected only Nazi voters and no one else in Germany
All political parties gained equally from the Depression's effects
The Depression had no real connection to the Nazis' rise in support
questions.answer: The Nazis directly blamed identifiable groups and promised concrete solutions, giving desperate voters a clear alternative other parties didn't offer
questions.why: The link isn't just timing — the Nazis actively exploited the crisis with scapegoating and simple promises that mainstream parties failed to match, converting despair into votes.
